proof:
Source. This is the supplied parent proof, Step 3(ii): 'Since |1 − ⟨e, ν⟩| = |⟨e, e − ν⟩| ≤ |ν − e| and φ∘η_r vanishes outside B_{rR}(x): |(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ φ(η_r(y))(1 − ⟨e, ν(y)⟩) dμ(y)| ≤ sup|φ|·(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_{rR}(x)} |ν − e| dμ = sup|φ|·Rⁿ·ε(rR) → 0. All integrals here are finite (bounded integrands supported in B_{rR}(x), μ(B_{rR}(x)) < ∞)'. This is parent Part 4(ii) with erratum E3 for Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3, chapter-03.txt lines 739-746: controlling ∫φ(1 − ν_{n+1})dμ_ρ needs a quantitative estimate on the measure. Here the excess decay ε(ρ) → 0 is a hypothesis; in the parent it is the output of the sibling density_estimates. The hypothesis μ(B_{ρ₁}(x)) < ∞ supplies integrability.

Notation. η_r := η_{x,r}, so η_r(y) = r⁻¹(y − x). Q(ρ) := (ρⁿ)⁻¹∫_{B_ρ(x)} |ν − e| dμ. D(r) := (rⁿ)⁻¹∫φ(η_r(y))dμ(y) − (rⁿ)⁻¹∫φ(η_r(y))⟨e, ν(y)⟩dμ(y).

1. Constants. φ is continuous with compact support, so there is M with |φ| ≤ M everywhere; in particular M ≥ 0. tsupport φ is compact, hence bounded, so it lies in some B_{R₀}(0) (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball). Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0; then tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0).

2. Localization. Let r > 0 and φ(η_r(y)) ≠ 0. Then η_r(y) ∈ tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0), and |η_r(y)| = r⁻¹|y − x|. So |y − x| < rR, i.e. y ∈ B_{rR}(x).

3. Integrability of the excess on small balls. For 0 < ρ ≤ ρ₁, μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B_{ρ₁}(x)) < ∞. The function y ↦ |ν(y) − e| is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (because ν is), and |ν(y) − e| ≤ |ν(y)| + |e| = 2 for μ-a.e. y. So it is bounded on a set of finite measure and hence μ-integrable on B_ρ(x) (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded).

4. The two integrals and their difference. Fix r ∈ (0, ρ₁/R) and put B := B_{rR}(x). Then rR < ρ₁, B is open (hence Borel), and μ(B) < ∞.
 - F(y) := φ(η_r(y)) is continuous (η_r is affine) with |F| ≤ M.
 - G(y) := φ(η_r(y))⟨e, ν(y)⟩ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: it is F times the composition of the continuous map v ↦ ⟨e, v⟩ with ν. Moreover |G| ≤ M|e||ν| = M μ-a.e.
 - By step 2 both vanish outside B (G(y) ≠ 0 forces φ(η_r(y)) ≠ 0).
 Being bounded on B with μ(B) < ∞ and zero off B, F and G are μ-integrable (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded, integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset). Therefore
 D(r) = (rⁿ)⁻¹∫(F − G)dμ = (rⁿ)⁻¹∫φ(η_r(y))(1 − ⟨e, ν(y)⟩)dμ(y) (mul_sub, integral_sub).

5. Pointwise bound. For every y, |F(y) − G(y)| ≤ 1_B(y)·M|ν(y) − e|.
 - If φ(η_r(y)) = 0, the left side is 0 and the right side is ≥ 0.
 - Otherwise y ∈ B by step 2. Since ⟨e, e⟩ = |e|² = 1, F(y) − G(y) = φ(η_r(y))(⟨e, e⟩ − ⟨e, ν(y)⟩) = φ(η_r(y))⟨e, e − ν(y)⟩. By Cauchy-Schwarz, |F(y) − G(y)| ≤ M|e||e − ν(y)| = M|ν(y) − e|.

6. Estimate. By step 3 the majorant 1_B·M|ν − e| is integrable (integrable_indicator_iff), and its integral is M∫_B|ν − e|dμ (integral_indicator, integral_const_mul). By norm_integral_le_of_norm_le and step 5, using (rⁿ)⁻¹ = Rⁿ((rR)ⁿ)⁻¹,
 |D(r)| ≤ (rⁿ)⁻¹ M ∫_{B_{rR}(x)} |ν − e| dμ = M Rⁿ Q(rR) for every r ∈ (0, ρ₁/R).

7. Limit. The map r ↦ rR is continuous, takes the value 0 at 0, and is positive for r > 0. So it maps 𝓝[>]0 into 𝓝[>]0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within). By hypothesis Q(rR) → 0 as r ↓ 0, hence M Rⁿ Q(rR) → 0. Since (0, ρ₁/R) ∈ 𝓝[>]0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), the bound of step 6 holds eventually. The squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero_norm') gives D(r) → 0 as r ↓ 0. ∎
key_steps: |φ| ≤ M and tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) with R = max(R₀, 1), so φ∘η_{x,r} vanishes off B_{rR}(x).
For r < ρ₁/R both integrands are bounded (|ν| = 1 μ-a.e.) and supported in B_{rR}(x), which has finite μ-measure, so both are integrable. Their difference is (rⁿ)⁻¹∫φ∘η_{x,r}(1 − ⟨e, ν⟩)dμ.
|1 − ⟨e, ν⟩| = |⟨e, e − ν⟩| ≤ |ν − e| gives |difference| ≤ M Rⁿ Q(rR), where Q(ρ) = (ρⁿ)⁻¹∫_{B_ρ(x)}|ν − e|dμ.
r ↦ rR maps 𝓝[>]0 into 𝓝[>]0, so Q(rR) → 0. Conclude by the squeeze theorem.
